One issue that has not yet been addressed, but which will be of great importance to Austria and its people, and which is particularly topical in these days, is the enlargement of the European Union. These days there will be regular – practically every week – votes, referendums in the candidate countries: Last week, on Saturday and Sunday, in Poland, with a great result – more than a three-quarters majority voted for accession. In the weekend, the Czech Republic is on the line. Slovakia, Hungary and Slovenia, our other neighbours, have already voted with Yes. I would like to warmly congratulate these neighbouring countries, but also all the other countries, among the ten candidate countries, on this great success for a European path, for all the work behind it, in order to make these countries eligible at all. I am proud and happy that we, as the Federal Government, have been able to participate in this and have thus created the conditions within Austria for this accession to be a real success for us and for the candidate countries. [[Congratulations on the ÖVP and the Freeman.]] Of course, I wish that the result in the Czech Republic is just as great, because for us Austrians this is, of course, a very important event. We are countries that have had to deal with major historical problems and still have to: Austria was both victims in the time of the Third Reich, but there were also enough Austrians as perpetrators on the road, especially in our neighbouring country. This should not be kept silent, nor be turned under the carpet of history, of historical oblivion. ParlaMint-AT_2003-06-10-022-XXII-NRSITZ-00020_d7e17435	Mr President. Gentlemen of the Federal Government! High house! The improvement of employment opportunities for people over 50 is an area in which we urgently need to take action. An important aspect – Mr Drinkl pointed out – is the reduction of the additional wage costs for workers, as the high cost of course is a barrier to the redeployment and further employment of employees, especially in economically difficult times. Therefore, the unemployment insurance contribution for women from 56 and men over 58 years of age will be reduced by 6 percentage points. Under Action 60 plus, additional labour costs are even reduced by a total of 12 percentage points, which will certainly be a clear incentive for older people to work. A total of €140 million will relieve the Austrian economy of these measures, thus creating new jobs. Everyone of us should be keenly interested in this. The special protection against termination for the elderly is relativized in the sense of these persons. From the practical experience it is absolutely useful to provide for a gender-neutral recast of this provision and to increase the malus for those employers who release older workers. In order to better protect those concerned from termination, the duration of the operation will also be used for the calculation of the malus amount in the future. Therefore, it will be significantly more expensive in future to exempt older workers with long-term employment. It will no longer, as before, be cheaper to release a 55-year-old woman to an equally old man, precisely because the age of life is assessed independently of sex. However, in order not to make it difficult for older people to recruit companies because of these important protective measures, the protection against dismissal for persons aged 50 and over, who are newly recruited, will only fall from the third year of employment. So far, special protective measures have already been applied with the sixth month of employment, which in practice has unfortunately led to the recruitment of these people under the same conditions. The instrument of part-time work has developed into a very important labour market policy measure and is therefore reformed. For those who can no longer go to early retirement due to the increase in the age of accession, the so-called oldage allowance is introduced with a 25 percent supplement to unemployment benefit. The key data are known, but I find one quite interesting and worth mentioning in this context. The average pension due to long unemployment is € 14 times € 727, so a total of € 10 178 per year. On the other hand, the average age transition fee will amount to € 12 times 1 083 per year, which is about €13 000 per year. This means, therefore, an average of €2 822 more per year for those concerned in the period prior to retirement. In addition, it is a benefit from unemployment insurance, which is therefore counted as a replacement period and is therefore an additional pension increase. Now I wonder if that means better or worse. I have already said at the beginning that the working world is changing. A key aspect of this is continuing vocational training. In addition to the extension of unemployment benefit in the case of qualification measures for all unemployed, we therefore create a legal right for persons seeking employment over 50 years of age for qualification measures. This is certainly an important step towards improving opportunities for older people. However, there is also a need for effective implementation of these sensible provisions by the respective labour market service. Especially when I look at the AMS Vienna, there is still a lot to do. We need to raise the actual retirement age clearly. That is, I think, absolutely undisputed. However, we must also help these people to be able to work longer. We do so with the measures provided for here.

The fourth point is too imprecise for us, since we want to see what that looks like in concrete implementation. The reason why we then reject it at the third reading is, above all, that we do not understand, criticize, criticize the procedure and the deadline. In the future, there will be no more double accounts of contribution periods. Political pensioners will have to make a solid contribution of 8 per cent until the ASVG maximum contribution base, and a 15 per cent solidarity contribution for an additional amount. The retirement age for old politicians will be increased to 65 years by 2017. Old politicians, who during the transitional period – and this is an essential point! - before the 65th. And if you look at the ASVG, it's almost equal. Ladies and gentlemen! You see, on this issue too, the liberal manuscript is visible.
